subtitle: Tapa remembers Frikooso hill
answer: Frikooso Afahye is the festival of the Akan-speaking Tapa people of the Biakoye District in the Oti Region, kept with their neighbours. It remembers the bravery and sacrifice of their ancestors at the battle of Frikooso, a low hill near Tapa Abotoase, the traditional capital. It is listed for October.

sections.title: The story
sections.html:
As the Tapa tell it, an Asante army first came against them and was driven back with stones rolled down from their mountain. A larger army returned. The deciding battle was fought at Frikooso, a low hill about three kilometres north of Tapa Abotoase, by Tapa with Worawora, Buem, Bowiri, Asato and other allies. It was the bloodiest in Tapa history, and the allies won.[[1]]

The festival honours the ancestors who fought and died for the land and its freedom.[[1]] The name Tapa itself comes from the flat-topped mountain where they first settled.[[1]]

sections.title: What happens
sections.html:
Tapa Abotoase, the traditional capital, is known for the festival.[[2]] Published accounts do not describe its programme.

Published accounts of Frikooso Afahye are short. If you know the festival, tell us more and we’ll add it.

sections.title: Good to know if you go
tips: Where: Tapa Abotoase is the traditional capital of the Tapa area, in the Biakoye District. See the Oti page for places nearby.
Check the dates: the traditional council sets them each year. Local radio and the national press carry the announcement.
Respect the rites: some rituals are sacred and not for cameras. Ask before photographing chiefs, priests or anyone taking part, and follow what the ushers ask.
